# Arbitrary integer rank: exact radial triangle Schur descent

This is a local theorem for an actual compatible family of homothetic planar triangle fibers. It proves an exact rank formula, all-normal and all-source optimality, and a complete finite ownership cover with genuine critical slack groups. Its baseline normalized depth is 4/9, so it is an above-target calibration for every positive integer dimension. It is not an OC theorem or a parity bound on the number of groups.

The three- and five-fiber calculations in `candidate 0e4cb84a76d46e82` and `candidate c42a2f528cc38b0c` are special cases. The new assertion is arbitrary integer rank, with a precise null complement and no unproved competing-source or compact-normal step.

## 1. Statement and actual bodies

Let B be a compact convex body in R^n and let

    P=B intersect Z^n

be centrally symmetric, finite, and contain 0. Let r^0:B -> (0,infinity) be continuous and concave, and suppose its sampled values obey r^0_z=r^0_-z. Put

    T=conv{(-1,-1),(2,-1),(-1,2)},   V=area(T)=9/2,
    C_r={(z,x): z in B, x in r(z)T}.

Every positive continuous concave r on B defines an actual convex body C_r in R^(n+2). Indeed, convex combinations of points of r(z)T lie in the appropriately weighted homothetic triangle, and concavity of r supplies the remaining inclusion. Compactness and nonempty interior follow from the hypotheses. Its COMPLETE integer fibers are exactly r_z T for z in P, each with positive area. Therefore q=2 and the intrinsic measure is exactly the sum of these areas.

Write

    L=span(P),  k=dim L,  G=sum_(z in P) z z^T,
    R(r)=sum_z r_z^2,  b(r)=sum_z r_z z,
    W(r)=b(r)^T G^dagger b(r),  E(r)=R(r)-W(r).       (1)

Here G^dagger is the inverse of G on L and zero on L-perp. In particular b always belongs to its range. If P={0}, all integer-normal terms below are absent and W=0.

There is a neighborhood of the sampled array r^0 such that EVERY compatible positive concave r in this neighborhood has

    max_(y in C_r intersect (Z^n x R^2)) raw_depth(y)
       = raw_depth(0,0)=2 E(r).                       (2)

The unique global maximizing point is (0,0). The three actual minimizing caps at this point are

    u_i.x - 2 (G^dagger b).z >= 0,
    u_1=(1,0), u_2=(0,1), u_3=(-1,-1).               (3)

Normal directions are understood modulo positive scaling and integer-normal components in L-perp, which do not change any trace on S. There are no other minimizing traces near this baseline.

Let R_0=R(r^0) and Q_0=2R_0. Scale all continuous coordinates by

    c(r)^2=R_0/E(r).                                  (4)

The scaled body is an actual convex body with the same complete integer base P and global raw depth exactly Q_0. Its total mixed area is

    M_tilde(r)=V R_0 + V R_0 W(r)/E(r).                (5)

Thus the fixed-depth mass gain is positive exactly when b(r) is nonzero. Every other source base admits an attained critical three-cap circuit whose caps have mass strictly below 2E(r); assign that circuit only its own base. Together with the group (3), assigned only base 0, these are a complete actual finite ownership cover. No group is required to cover every base.

## 2. The finite-base bounded-tilt lemma

The following elementary fact makes attainment and uniform compactness explicit. It does not assume regularity of the polytope vertices or a selected minimizing sequence.

Fix a finite base P and a source z_0 in P. Suppose all continuous fibers lie strictly inside a fixed Euclidean ball of radius H, and the source continuous coordinate is zero. A nonvertical through-source cap can be written

    u.x + alpha.(z-z_0) >= 0,  |u|=1.

There is a constant K depending only on P and z_0 such that its traces on all fibers can be preserved by some integer coefficient beta with |beta|<=K H.

Proof. Work in span{z-z_0:z in P}, since perpendicular coefficients have no effect. For each d_z=z-z_0 with |alpha.d_z|<=H, impose the equality beta.d_z=alpha.d_z. For the other bases impose beta.d_z>=H or beta.d_z<=-H according to the sign of alpha.d_z. This is a nonempty closed polyhedron, since alpha is feasible. All right sides have absolute value at most H. Its minimum-norm point beta exists. It is orthogonal to every direction annihilating all equality rows and all active inequality rows: both signs of a sufficiently short motion in such a direction are feasible. Thus beta lies in the span of the active rows. Select an independent subfamily I spanning them. If D_I is its row matrix and t_I its right-side vector, then

    beta=D_I^T (D_I D_I^T)^(-1) t_I.

There are only finitely many such independent row families from the fixed vectors d_z (and their negatives). Their inverse norms give the required constant K. If the row span is zero, beta=0. Equalities preserve every nonsaturated trace, while inequalities at or beyond +/-H give exactly the same full or empty trace, because H is a strict support bound. This proves the assertion.

The same constant can be chosen for all source bases by taking a maximum over the finite P. With |u|=1 the resulting normal parameter set is compact. Cap mass is continuous there for positive planar fibers: a convergent cap indicator can fail to converge only on its limiting line, which has area zero in each fiber.

A vertical through-source cap cannot improve the infimum. Choose any nonzero continuous normal u, multiply the original integer normal by a sufficiently large finite factor, and use this u. All bases with nonzero projected integer value have the same full or empty status. The bases on the original vertical boundary now have a subset of their previous full trace. At the centroid source itself this is a proper subset of positive area, so the replacement is strictly cheaper. Therefore the infimum over ALL ambient caps at a fiber centroid is attained by a nonvertical cap in the compact representation above. A containing halfspace can first be translated to pass through the source, which can only reduce its mass.

For nearby sampled radii a single common H works. Moreover, for ANY fixed measurable halfspace H', uniformly over all its normal coefficients,

    |mu_r(H')-mu_s(H')| <= V sum_z |r_z^2-s_z^2|.     (6)

Indeed, positive homothetic copies r_z T and s_z T are nested, because 0 is in the interior of T. The right side is exactly the measure of their disjoint-fiber symmetric difference. Thus the raw depths at fixed centroids are continuous uniformly in the normal family.

## 3. The exact baseline and its complete active menu

We use the fully proved triangle paired-depth lemma in `candidate 4ffd81a5b3e6f9fb`: for a triangle A, its centroid g, any nonzero u, and any real t,

    |A intersect {u.x>=u.g+t}|
      + |A intersect {u.x>=u.g-t}| >= (8/9)|A|.       (7)

That source proves the stronger all-point identity, by explicit piecewise quadratic tails, with all full, empty, supporting, and repeated-height cases. Only its centroid case is used here. Ordinary centroid depth of a triangle is 4/9, with equality exactly at the three vertex caps parallel to the opposite edge. For completeness, a one-vertex cap through the centroid has intercepts s,t with 1/(3s)+1/(3t)=1, so st>=4/9 by AM-GM, with equality only at s=t=2/3. A two-vertex cap has area at least 1/2. This also identifies every equality direction.

At Y=(0,0), pair each z with -z. Their equal triangles see opposite threshold displacements for EVERY integer tilt. Equation (7), plus the own ordinary triangle bound, gives

    raw_depth(Y)>=2 sum_z (r^0_z)^2=Q_0.             (8)

The canonical cylindrical caps u_i.x>=0 attain this value. They cover every fiber space, so their common mass also bounds the depth of EVERY point from above. Hence the baseline global raw maximum is Q_0.

Equality in (8) first requires a canonical continuous normal, because the own fiber at base 0 has positive area. For a canonical direction in an equal-radius pair, put s=|alpha.z|. Its two cap masses sum to

    4r_z^2+s^2              if 0<=s<=r_z,
    (9/2)r_z^2+(2r_z-s)^2/2 if r_z<=s<=2r_z,
    (9/2)r_z^2              if s>=2r_z.              (9)

The sum is strictly larger than 4r_z^2 unless s=0. Thus equality requires alpha.z=0 for every z in P, equivalently alpha has zero projection on L. These are exactly the three traces stated in (3) at the baseline. The compact representation in Section 2 then supplies a strictly positive mass gap outside arbitrary small neighborhoods of these three active trace directions.

## 4. Every other source has a genuine strict gap

The linear map A(x,y)=(-x-y,x) cyclically permutes the triangle vertices, preserves area, satisfies A^3=I, and I+A+A^2=0. It acts simultaneously on every fiber of every radial family considered here. Halfspace depth has convex superlevel sets: a halfspace containing a convex combination contains at least one of the combined points, hence has at least their common depth lower bound. Averaging the orbit of any point within a fiber therefore proves

    raw_depth(z,x)<=raw_depth(z,0)                   (10)

for every original point in every fiber.

Fix z_0!=0. A canonical cylinder through (z_0,0) still has mass Q_0. Perturb it to

    x+alpha.(z-z_0)>=0.

All its finitely many traces are proper for alpha sufficiently small. The exact vertex-cap formula is

    (1/2) sum_z [2r^0_z+alpha.(z-z_0)]^2.

Its derivative at alpha=0 is

    2 sum_z r^0_z(z-z_0)
       = -2 z_0 sum_z r^0_z,                         (11)

where evenness and symmetry give sum r^0_z z=0. Taking alpha=t z_0 for small t>0 strictly lowers the mass. Therefore every nonzero source centroid, and by (10) every point in its fiber, has depth strictly below Q_0. There are finitely many source bases, so the gap is uniform over all nonzero bases. Equation (6) preserves a positive gap for nearby radial arrays.

An explicit positive gap is available if desired. Put S_1=sum_z r^0_z, r_min=min_z r^0_z, d_z=z_0.(z-z_0), J=max_z |d_z|, and H_2=sum_z d_z^2. Since 0 is in P and z_0!=0, J and H_2 are positive. Choose

    t=min{r_min/(2J), S_1 |z_0|^2/H_2}.

Every cut stays in the proper chamber because |t d_z|<=r_min/2. Its exact mass is Q_0-2t S_1 |z_0|^2+(t^2/2)H_2, at most Q_0-(3/2)t S_1 |z_0|^2. Taking the minimum of these positive decreases over the finite nonzero source bases gives a literal common gap, without an assumption of smooth source maximizers.

At base 0, any x!=0 has some u_i.x>0. Translate that baseline canonical cap up to pass through (0,x). It loses a positive area subset of the own fiber, so the depth is strictly below Q_0. Thus Y is the unique baseline global maximizer.

## 5. The exact optimized normal formula

Restrict integer coefficients to L. In the chart around u_1=(1,0), write the through-Y cap as

    x+theta y+alpha.z>=0.

For every sufficiently nearby radial array and normal parameters, every trace remains in its original proper one-vertex chamber. Direct edge intersection gives the EXACT actual mass

    Phi(r,alpha,theta)
       = sum_z [(2-theta)r_z+alpha.z]^2/[2(1-theta)]. (12)

Completing the square on L yields

    Phi = [(2-theta)^2/(2(1-theta))] E(r)
      + [(alpha+(2-theta)G^dagger b)^T G
          (alpha+(2-theta)G^dagger b)]/[2(1-theta)]. (13)

E(r)>0 near the baseline. Since

    (2-theta)^2/(1-theta)=4+theta^2/(1-theta),

the unique nearby minimizer is

    theta=0, alpha=-2G^dagger b, Phi=2E(r).           (14)

At the baseline its normal Hessian is diag(G|L,R_0), positive definite. Cyclic symmetry gives the identical result in the other two canonical charts.

These local minima are global over all normal directions. Use the common compact normal representation from Section 2; at the baseline the only minima are the three in Section 3. Away from their chart neighborhoods there is a positive compact gap, preserved by the uniform estimate (6). Within smaller chart neighborhoods, positive definite Hessians persist and (13) gives the unique minimum. Shrink the body neighborhood so the displayed optimizers stay inside those neighborhoods. Hence (14) is the true all-normal depth at Y and (3) is the complete active trace menu. No local stationary point is being promoted to a global minimum without the gap argument.

At any middle point x!=0, one of the three caps (3) can be shifted through x and strictly decrease its own-fiber contribution, as in Section 4. The nonzero-base gaps from Section 4 persist, while (14) tends to Q_0. Consequently Y remains the unique global maximizing point, proving (2).

## 6. Genuine slack source circuits and exact ownership

At every nonzero z_0, Section 2 gives an actual depth-attaining nonvertical cap through (z_0,0), say

    u.x+alpha.(z-z_0)>=0.

Apply the three area-preserving cyclic maps. All three resulting caps have the SAME actual critical mass D(z_0,0)<D(0,0), the same integer coefficient alpha, and continuous normals whose sum is zero and which span the plane. They are a positive full-rank continuous-normal circuit. At base z_0 their three halfspaces cover all of R^2: if all three defining expressions were negative, their sum would be negative although that sum is zero. Assign this group only the base z_0. The main group (3) is assigned only base 0 and has the same exact coverage property there. This covers every original fiber with finitely many groups and strict budget slack at every auxiliary group.

One may freeze the baseline auxiliary groups when constructing a smooth nearby covering menu: their incidence and own-base coverage remain exact, while strict cap-budget slack persists by (6). These frozen caps need not remain depth-critical. Alternatively, reselect an attained critical cap at each nearby source and take its orbit; then every auxiliary group consists of actual critical caps at the current body. No smooth choice of these slack minimizing normals is required or asserted.

There is also a useful strict drift sign: since an auxiliary critical cap has mass below the actual depth at Y, it cannot contain Y. Hence

    alpha.z_0>0.                                    (15)

This is an actual geometric consequence, not an assigned free moment. No cardinality bound smaller than |P| is claimed. Different source circuits may contain shared planes; they retain their one original mass and are not varied as fictitious independent copies.

## 7. Exact rank, null complement, and admissible affine escapes

The common continuous homothety in (4) preserves the lattice, all halfspaces, full integer fiber membership, and scales every cap mass by c(r)^2. Since the current true global maximum is 2E(r), its scaled value is Q_0. The total area is V R(r), yielding (5). All selected slack groups remain strictly below the same Q_0 after scaling; their integer coefficients scale by c(r), preserving incidence and ownership.

For a sampled-array velocity v=(v_z), put m(v)=sum_z v_z z. At an even baseline b=0, equation (5) gives the fixed-depth mass Hessian

    2V m(v)^T G^dagger m(v).                         (16)

It is positive semidefinite with rank k on the full sampled-array space, and kernel exactly

    {v: sum_z v_z z=0}.                              (17)

These are exact statements about the normal-optimized, normalized geometry. They are not claims about the raw volume Hessian, which also counts the null directions before cap normalization.

All k affine directions are genuinely available within the actual body family, without strict concavity of the initial radius. For a in L small, take

    r_a(z)=r^0(z)+a.z  on the entire projection B.

Concavity is preserved by adding an affine function. Positivity persists uniformly because B is compact and min_B r^0>0. Its sampled values satisfy

    b(r_a)=G a,
    R(r_a)=R_0+a^T G a,
    E(r_a)=R_0.                                      (18)

Thus no scaling is even needed: the actual global raw depth stays EXACTLY Q_0, while the actual total mixed area increases by V a^T G a, strictly for every a!=0 in L. These affine velocities are volume-neutral to first order separately in every lattice parity class. Indeed, z and -z lie in the same parity class and have equal baseline radii, so their first-volume derivatives cancel. The statement does not infer a parity index theorem: it only records a property of these explicit admissible velocities.

If a perturbation has b(r)=0, equation (5) gives EXACT equality after normalization, not merely a vanishing second derivative. Its normalized maximum depth remains 4/9. General perturbations have

    normalized maximum depth = (4/9)[1-W(r)/R(r)].   (19)

This strict decrease for W>0 occurs near the above-target baseline 4/9. It gives no assertion that an arbitrary hypothetical below-OC variational maximizer has this radial symmetry, these slack sources, or this compatible affine escape.

## 8. Boundary scope

All sampled fibers here have positive planar area, so all nonvertical boundaries have zero measure; supporting and saturated cuts were retained in the bounded-tilt and paired-tail arguments. Purely vertical cuts were explicitly dominated rather than discarded without explanation. No approximation or change of integer coordinates is used. Rank-deficient sampled bases use L and G^dagger, so invisible integer-normal directions create no false strict Hessian. The case P={0} is the ordinary triangle case with rank zero and no slack groups. For n=0 the same convention gives the identical ordinary statement. The current theorem fixes continuous dimension two and does not settle arbitrary-dimensional OC.
